_note: RC-1 (OPP-0003) placeholder answers for Crown Technical Systems (P-49 part B). ILLUSTRATIVE, not real Crown or Flex positions: no rating, test result or certification here is verified.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: We would supply 15 kV-class metal-clad switchgear with arc-resistant Type 2B construction, draw-out vacuum breakers, protective relays, instrument transformers, a control power transformer and battery-backed DC control power, housed in a walk-in E-House with fire-rated walls of at least 2 hours. Main and feeder ratings and the short-circuit rating for 1 s will be stated from the Owner's load schedule once our short-circuit study is done.
answers.conditions: Ratings depend on the Owner's load schedule and the utility fault level.
answers.next_steps: Request the load schedule and utility fault data during the dialogue; run the short-circuit study.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: The lineup can be built for a short-circuit withstand within the 18 to 40 kA range at 13.8 kV, with the duration stated after our study, and it works with either low-resistance or solid MV grounding. The 110 kV basic impulse level is above the standard level for 15 kV-class gear, so we propose a change to reach it.
answers.reason: Standard 15 kV-class metal-clad switchgear is rated below 110 kV BIL.
answers.workaround: Supply the 13.8 kV lineup with 27 kV-class breakers, bus insulation and instrument transformers so the equipment meets at least 110 kV BIL, confirmed in design review.
answers.next_steps: Confirm the BIL basis with the Owner and price the 27 kV-class insulation option.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: We would supply one 15 kV-class switchgear lineup per deployment unit, six in total, each feeding that unit's power blocks and built to the same L1.04 to L1.06 specification. Each lineup is factory-assembled and tested in its E-House to shorten site work.

Illustrative placeholder response: Our switchgear is designed to operate across the 13.8 kV plus or minus 10%, 57 to 63 Hz envelope of the Lot 1 to Lot 2 interface, including the switching and fault events foreseeable within it. We confirm this for the MV interface we supply; disturbances on the DC and cooling interfaces are covered by the units supplying those lots.
answers.conditions: Confirmed for the MV interface Crown supplies; the DC and cooling interfaces are confirmed by the units supplying those lots, and the foreseeable disturbances are agreed in a joint coordination study.
answers.next_steps: Run a joint protection coordination and transient study with the power block supplier.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: For our scope we meet the Lot 1 to Lot 2 interface at 13.8 kV, three-phase three-wire plus PE, with low-resistance or solid grounding, can provide the optional 4.16 kV chiller bus, and our relay and metering panels report to Lot 6 over Modbus TCP/IP. The DC, busway, rack and cooling interfaces are answered by the units supplying them.
answers.conditions: Crown answers IF-02, the 4.16 kV option of IF-08 and the switchgear side of IF-09 only.
answers.next_steps: Agree the Modbus register map with the Lot 6 supplier.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: We accept that the Owner furnishes some major equipment, and we will coordinate the switchgear interfaces, protection settings and drawings with it so it fits the overall design.
answers.conditions: Owner-furnished equipment data is provided in time for the design freeze.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: We will provide operator and maintenance training for the switchgear and E-Houses, covering safe switching, breaker racking and routine maintenance, at the factory and on site.
answers.next_steps: Agree the number of trainees and sessions per deployment unit.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: Noted. We will use the Owner's published PUE and energy price to state the switchgear losses and their cost over the system's life in our total cost of ownership input.

Illustrative placeholder response: We will support the switchgear for five years from acceptance, 24 by 7, with a four-hour response through our field service team, and the draw-out design allows concurrent maintenance one section at a time. Most repairs can be done within 2 hours by swapping a breaker from on-site spares, but repairs to the fixed bus need a planned outage.
answers.reason: A 2-hour repair time cannot be met for faults on the fixed bus or bus compartments.
answers.workaround: Apply the 2-hour target to draw-out breakers and relays, with spare breakers held on site; set a separate planned-outage window for fixed-bus repairs, which the redundant lineup arrangement allows.
answers.next_steps: Agree the on-site spares list with the Owner.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: We will deliver the switchgear in phases, one deployment unit at a time, with each lineup on site and energised ahead of the core components and test system it feeds.

Illustrative placeholder response: Each lineup goes through factory tests, witnessed if the Owner wishes, then site tests at commissioning, and our engineers support the 30-day availability test. Our deliverables will be timed against award and first delivery.

Illustrative placeholder response: We will agree the switchgear factory test plan at least 30 days before the factory test, including fault injection such as loss of control power, relay trip tests by secondary injection and breaker operation checks. Burn-in and benchmarks apply to the compute systems, not to switchgear.
answers.reason: Burn-in and benchmark runs are not applicable to MV switchgear.
answers.next_steps: Share a draft factory test plan with the Owner.

Illustrative placeholder response: Our switchgear work follows the three phases: installed and integrated, validated by site testing, then supported through operational readiness.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: We accept liquidated damages for missed service levels, capped by the at-risk amounts described, and delay penalties that scale with the length of the delay and the seriousness of the breach, subject to an aggregate cap on liquidated damages and delay penalties together.
answers.reason: Liquidated damages and delay penalties have no overall limit as written, which leaves an open-ended risk on a phased multi-lot delivery.
answers.workaround: An aggregate cap on liquidated damages and delay penalties together, set as a percentage of each lot's price; the percentage is stated in the financial offer and listed in the commercial exceptions schedule (CT-08).

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: Our commercial exceptions are listed in the separate exceptions schedule and kept to a minimum: on liquidated damages, only the aggregate cap per lot asked for under CT-07; any indexed price is shown there only as an alternative to the firm price.

Illustrative placeholder response: Our switchgear warranty is included within the five-year maintenance period, and we take responsibility for failures caused by disturbances foreseeable within the Section 9 interface limits.
answers.conditions: Disturbances outside the stated interface limits are excluded.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: We provide a supply-chain security and risk plan for the switchgear, with qualified alternative sources and mitigation for sensitive parts such as relays and breaker electronics. Instead of a guarantee for each original component over the system's whole lifetime, we commit to the availability period stated as the proposed change.
answers.reason: No supplier can guarantee every original component for an open-ended system lifetime: electronic parts follow their makers' life cycles.
answers.workaround: Spare parts or compatible form-fit-function replacements available for at least 10 years from acceptance, with at least 12 months' notice of end of life and a last-time-buy offer before any component is discontinued.
